# Use Alexa+ to Capture Meeting Action Items by Voice

> **In short:** Alexa+ does not listen to or record your whole meeting — it only hears what you say to it after "Alexa". What it can do is remember the points you tell it, add tasks to your to-do list, set reminders and recap your conversation with it. That makes it a quick, private way to catch action items by voice.

You're already comfortable talking to Alexa+ for music, timers, or quick questions. This guide shows one more useful habit for work: whenever a decision or a task comes up in a meeting, you say it to Alexa+ in one sentence. By the end of the meeting, your action items are already on your to-do list — and you never had to switch windows to write them down.

## Before you start
- An **Amazon account** with **Alexa+** and an Echo device (or the Alexa app) signed in. You should already know how to say "Alexa, …" and get a response.
- **An Echo that only you use, if possible.** Amazon's help says notes saved with Alexa+ are available to anyone using an Alexa device logged into your account — so don't save confidential work details on a family Echo.
- **A heads-up for the others:** a short "I'm using Alexa to note my action items" avoids surprises when you talk to it.
- About **15 minutes** for your first run.

## Step 1 — Know what Alexa+ will and won't hear
Alexa+ wakes up when you say "Alexa" and responds to what follows. It does not quietly take minutes of everything people say. So the method is simple: **you** decide what's worth keeping and say it out loud, one short sentence at a time. Keep your sentences to who, what and when — they're easier for Alexa to catch and easier for you to check later.

💬 Example: "Sam sends the budget draft by Friday."

You'll know it worked when you have a short list of the kinds of things you'll capture: decisions, tasks with a name, and deadlines.

## Step 2 — Ask Alexa+ to remember each decision
Amazon's **Remember This** feature for Alexa+ stores information you ask it to keep. When a decision is made, say **"Alexa, remember that…"** followed by your sentence. Amazon's own examples are as simple as "Remember my friend's birthday" — the same works for a work point.

💬 Example: say *"Alexa, remember that the Q2 launch moves to June 12."*

You'll know it worked when Alexa confirms it will remember it.

## Step 3 — Put the tasks on your to-do list
For anything that is a task rather than a fact, add it straight to a list. Say **"Alexa, add … to my to-do list."** Each task becomes its own entry that you can check off later in the Alexa app or by voice. If a task has a deadline, you can also ask for a reminder.

💬 Example: say *"Alexa, add 'send budget draft to Sam' to my to-do list,"* then *"Alexa, remind me on Thursday at 10 a.m. to send the budget draft."*

You'll know it worked when Alexa confirms each item, and the tasks appear on your to-do list in the Alexa app.

## Step 4 — Get your points back after the meeting
When the meeting ends, ask Alexa+ what it stored. Amazon's help lists questions like **"What did I ask you to remember last week?"** — you can ask about today or about a topic instead. If something changed, ask about it and then tell Alexa to change it, just like Amazon's "change my son's shoe size to 7" example.

💬 Example: say *"Alexa, what did I ask you to remember today about the Q2 launch?"*

You'll know it worked when Alexa reads back the points you saved.

## Step 5 — Ask for a recap or a follow-up email
Amazon says you can ask Alexa+ to **recap your discussion** and send it to the Alexa app or your email, and that it can help you write emails and adjust their tone. Ask for a short recap of what you told it, or a draft follow-up you can review before anything is sent.

💬 Example: *"Alexa, recap what I told you about the Q2 launch and send it to my email."*

You'll know it worked when the recap arrives in the Alexa app or your inbox.

## Step 6 — Review and clean up at the end of the day
Open the Alexa app and check your to-do list. Amazon's help says you can also go to and archive your **Remember This** notes in the Alexa app — archive anything you no longer need, and correct any name Alexa misheard. This 60-second habit is what makes the whole method trustworthy.

You'll know it worked when your to-do list holds only real tasks, and old meeting points are archived.

## Common mistakes
- **Expecting Alexa+ to take minutes for you.** It only hears what you say to it. If you want a full record of the meeting, use a proper meeting tool — Alexa+ is for your own action items.
- **Saving confidential details on a shared Echo.** Notes are available to anyone using an Alexa device logged into your account. Keep sensitive details out of it, or use a device only you use.
- **Long, rambling sentences.** "Sam, budget draft, Friday" survives much better than a 40-word thought. Short sentences are easier for Alexa to catch and for you to check.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** the same habit works at home — say a to-do out loud during a family call, and it's on your list before you hang up.
- **For your business or work:** in a one-on-one or a small recurring meeting, you stay engaged in the conversation, and your action items are already waiting on your to-do list when the meeting ends.
- **If you want to go further:** ask Alexa+ to set reminders for each deadline you mentioned, so nothing depends on you remembering to check the list.

## Try it now
In your next meeting — even a 15-minute one — capture just two things: one decision with "Alexa, remember that…" and one task with "Alexa, add … to my to-do list." Afterwards, ask "Alexa, what did I ask you to remember today?" You'll see in under ten minutes whether the habit fits how you work.
